newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African diplomats grapple with rights issues.
newsitem.headline: S.African diplomats grapple with rights issues.

text.p: South Africa cannot satisfy over-ambitious expectations that it will champion human rights causes around the world, a senior diplomat said on Monday.

"Precisely because we have carried this human rights torch, the expectation is that we are going to speak about each and every human rights violation wherever it rears its head," Tebogo Mafole, a deputy director general in the foreign affairs department, told a parliamentary committee.

"We haven't been able to live up to the expectations," he said, citing President Nelson Mandela's trip to Southeast Asia earlier this month during which he was criticised for not taking Burma to task over human rights.
Another foreign affairs official Lesley Labuschagne told the committee that South Africa was involved in a secret initiative over Burma, but declined to give details in public.
Mandela, who won the Nobel peace prize in 1993 for his role in defeating apartheid, has committed his government to making human rights a cornerstone of foreign policy.
But Anthony Mongalo, responsible for Africa within the foreign affairs department, said this was a difficult policy to interpret.
"In the Far East, their concept of human rights is different to ours. How do we impose our standards on others?" he asked.

Citing a row with the United States earlier this year over proposals to sell arms to Syria, Mongalo said if South Africa refused to sell weapons to countries that violated human rights, "you sell to nowhere".
